root_cause.text: In `net/core/skbuff.c`, `pskb_carve_inside_header()` and `pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear()` `memcpy()` the old `skb_shared_info` including `destructor_arg` for MSG_ZEROCOPY skbs but failed to take an extra `net_zcopy_get()` reference for the copied `uarg`, causing the zerocopy refcount to underflow and free `ubuf_info_msgzc` while live TX skbs still reference it.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (skb_zcopy(skb)) net_zcopy_get(skb_zcopy(skb));` in both helpers, and the CVE text says the copied `shinfo->destructor_arg` was “without a refcount bump,” which “drive[s] uarg->refcnt to zero prematurely,” leading to use-after-free in `skb_release_data()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Retain the skb zero-copy context while carving packet data to prevent premature release of zero-copy resources.
intent_record.what: In pskb_carve_inside_header(), after successfully allocating new head data, the code now checks whether the skb uses zero-copy (`skb_zcopy(skb)`) and, if so, calls `net_zcopy_get(skb_zcopy(skb))` before incrementing fragment references.
intent_record.how: This adds a reference hold on the skb's zero-copy context when the packet is being carved and its fragments are being retained, preventing the zero-copy resources from being released too early and avoiding use-after-free or premature cleanup during later packet processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Preserve skb zero-copy backing ownership during nonlinear carving by taking a reference before releasing the skb data.
intent_record.what: In `pskb_carve_inside_nonlinear()`, two lines were added after the allocation failure check: if `skb_zcopy(skb)` is true, the code now calls `net_zcopy_get(skb_zcopy(skb))` before `skb_release_data(skb, SKB_CONSUMED)`.
intent_record.how: This increments the reference or usage count for the skb's zero-copy state before the skb data is released, preventing the zero-copy backing object from being freed too early while the skb is being carved and its head data replaced.

Releasing the skb data after carving is the point at which the copied shared_info/destructor_arg must remain valid; without first taking net_zcopy_get() on the copied uarg, this release can drop the last reference and underflow the zerocopy refcount.

vuln_statements.explanation: This carving path preserves fragment references, but it did not also take an extra reference on the copied MSG_ZEROCOPY destructor_arg/uarg. As a result, the copied zerocopy context could be freed while still referenced by live TX skbs.

This release point occurs after the skb shared_info has been copied, so the copied zerocopy destructor_arg/uarg must already have a refcount hold. Without a corresponding net_zcopy_get(), releasing the data can drop the last reference and underflow the zerocopy refcount.
